approvalRequirements: Be a Lakeland Electric residential customer for at least one year with a Good or Excellent utility credit rating and use the property as the applicant's primary residence.
Propose a currently eligible energy improvement and use a contractor accepted for the program.
Submit the customer and contractor applications, proposal, specifications, photographs, and required step sheet before work begins.
Execute and notarize the loan and lien documents before purchasing or installing the improvement.
Complete the approved work and pass Lakeland Electric's post-installation inspection before loan funds are released.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: Lakeland Electric currently accepts applications through an objective, first-come interest-free loan process. A qualifying homeowner who completes the required pre-work documents, lien closing, installation, and inspection is likely to be funded while program money remains available.
reviews.evidenceText: The active residential loan offers interest-free financing for qualifying homeowners, requires customer and contractor submissions before work, uses signed loan and lien documents, and releases funds after inspection.

approvalRequirements: Be an eligible Lane Electric member with the measure installed at a qualifying served property.
Purchase or install a measure covered by a current Lane Electric rebate and meet the applicable technical specifications.
Use the measure-specific application, contractor, purchase, or designated instant-rebate process.
Complete any required energy audit, advance authorization, or inspection for the selected measure.
Submit the required invoice, model, installation, and account documentation while program funds remain available.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: Lane Electric currently publishes prescriptive and instant-rebate pathways for qualifying residential measures. Eligible members who use the applicable channel and provide complete documentation are likely to receive the incentive after routine review.
reviews.evidenceText: Lane Electric's current residential offerings include heat-pump rebates, weatherization incentives, audits, and an instant heat-pump-water-heater rebate, with measure-specific applications and verification requirements.

approvalRequirements: Be an eligible Lane Electric member with a residential or commercial building served by the cooperative.
Complete the program's energy assessment or other required weatherization evaluation.
Limit the project to recommended, currently eligible efficiency or weatherization measures.
Obtain program authorization before beginning work when required by the selected incentive pathway.
Submit final invoices and installation documentation and pass any required completion inspection or verification.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: The current weatherization program uses an assessment and defined incentive process rather than competitive scoring. A member who completes approved recommended measures and passes closeout review is likely to receive the published grant or other incentive, subject to program limits.
reviews.evidenceText: Lane Electric currently offers weatherization assistance tied to recommended measures, including a cash grant and zero-interest financing, with energy assessments and program review supporting project eligibility.

approvalRequirements: Be an eligible Lane Electric member and install the heat pump at a qualifying served property.
Select equipment that meets the current heat-pump program specifications.
Submit the required program and contractor documentation before or after installation as directed.
For the loan option, complete Pacific Cascade Federal Credit Union membership and credit underwriting requirements.
Complete installation and any required inspection or documentation review before the rebate or loan proceeds are finalized.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: Lane Electric offers an objective cash-rebate path as well as a financing option. A technically qualifying installation is likely to receive the rebate after review, although the loan alternative separately depends on third-party credit approval.
reviews.evidenceText: The current heat-pump program offers an $800 rebate or zero-interest financing up to the published limit, with the financing option processed through Pacific Cascade Federal Credit Union.

approvalRequirements: Be an eligible Lane Electric residential member with a qualifying served home.
Complete the required energy audit or weatherization assessment and use the resulting recommended scope.
Obtain Lane Electric project authorization before beginning financed weatherization work.
Complete Pacific Cascade Federal Credit Union credit and membership underwriting for the loan.
Use approved work practices, submit final cost and installation records, and pass any required completion verification.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: The weatherization project can qualify under published program rules, but the loan is not an entitlement. Funding depends on project approval and borrower-specific credit underwriting by the participating credit union.
reviews.evidenceText: Lane Electric currently makes zero-interest weatherization loans available for recommended measures, while loan approval and disbursement require the participating credit union's financing process and project verification.

approvalRequirements: Be an eligible Lansing Board of Water & Light commercial or industrial customer for the project site.
Select a current prescriptive or custom electric-efficiency measure and satisfy the applicable equipment and savings specifications.
Obtain written preapproval before commitment for projects above the published threshold and for measures specifically designated for advance review.
Install the approved equipment within the authorization period.
Submit the final application, invoices, technical records, and other completion documents and allow inspection or verification before payment.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: The current business program is a prescriptive and custom incentive pathway rather than a competitively ranked grant. A qualifying project that obtains required preapproval and passes final document and installation review is likely to receive the incentive.
reviews.evidenceText: BWL currently offers commercial and industrial incentives for lighting, HVAC, refrigeration, compressed air, and custom equipment, with advance approval for designated projects and final verification before payment.

approvalRequirements: Be an eligible Lansing Board of Water & Light residential customer at the installation address.
Purchase and install a currently listed product or measure meeting the published efficiency and installation specifications.
Complete any required pre-inspection or advance approval for designated electrification or heat-pump measures.
Submit the current application with receipts, model information, contractor or installation records, and other measure-specific proof by the filing deadline.
Allow BWL to verify the account, product, and installation before payment while funds remain available.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: BWL's current residential rebates use objective product, customer, and documentation requirements and are offered first-come while funds last. A complete qualifying claim is likely to be paid after any required pre-inspection and routine verification.
reviews.evidenceText: BWL publishes current residential appliance, HVAC, heat-pump, thermostat, water-heating, and electrification incentives, with measure-specific specifications, filing deadlines, and pre-inspection for selected projects.

approvalRequirements: Be a current Lansing Board of Water & Light customer in good standing and install the charging equipment at an eligible service address.
Install a qualifying hardwired Level 2 charger and, for the published second-meter rebate, a dedicated secondary meter enrolled on the required rate.
Initiate the utility work request and load-information process and complete the preinstallation design review; obtain specific BWL approval for chargers above the published amperage threshold.
Complete required electrical permitting, inspection, meter work, and utility energization.
Submit the signed rebate application, Michigan vehicle registration, and charger and electrical-work invoices for final review.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: The current second-meter charger rebate follows a defined utility design, inspection, and claim process. A customer who completes the service requirements and submits the mandatory documentation is likely to receive the rebate after verification.
reviews.evidenceText: BWL currently offers a residential second-meter Level 2 charging rebate and requires account eligibility, utility design coordination, electrical inspection, rate enrollment, vehicle registration, and paid installation documentation.

approvalRequirements: Operate an eligible existing large commercial or industrial facility in New Jersey and meet the current Large Energy Users Program participation threshold.
Confirm facility and account eligibility with the program before developing the final project package.
Submit the required application, technical analysis, energy-savings calculations, scope, cost, and equipment documentation.
Receive program technical and incentive approval before implementation when required by the project process.
Complete the approved work and submit final invoices, commissioning, measurement, and verification records while funds remain available.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: The program is currently open and first-come, but each large custom project requires facility qualification and project-specific technical and economic review. Eligibility therefore provides an application path rather than a certain award.
reviews.evidenceText: New Jersey currently accepts Large Energy Users Program applications for customized efficiency upgrades in qualifying existing non-hospital commercial and industrial facilities on a first-come basis.

approvalRequirements: Develop a qualifying Nevada renewable-energy facility that meets the current technology, minimum capacity, operating-life, permitting, and business-license requirements.
Satisfy the applicable capital-investment, Nevada employment and residency, wage, health-insurance, and nonduplication requirements.
Submit a complete tax-abatement application with project, ownership, financial, employment, construction, and tax information.
Receive Governor's Office of Energy review and a favorable eligibility determination after the required public hearing.
Execute the tax-abatement agreement and pass annual compliance audits throughout the abatement period.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: The abatement is available only after a detailed statutory eligibility review, public hearing, and formal agreement, followed by continuing compliance. The substantial facility, investment, employment, and wage conditions make approval project-specific rather than automatic.
reviews.evidenceText: Nevada's current program requires a qualifying large renewable facility, detailed economic and workforce conditions, agency review, a public hearing, a formal abatement agreement, and annual compliance audits.

approvalRequirements: Be an eligible Lassen Municipal Utility District residential customer for the installation address.
Purchase and install a new product or system that appears on the current residential rebate list and meets the published efficiency specifications.
Submit the current rebate application with the paid receipt or invoice, model information, and required installation documentation.
Complete any contractor, permit, or inspection requirement applicable to the selected measure.
Allow LMUD to verify customer, product, and installation eligibility before payment while funds remain available.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: LMUD currently maintains an objective residential rebate process for listed appliances, heat-pump water heaters, and air-source heat pumps. A complete claim for a currently listed measure is likely to be paid, but several broader historical retrofit mappings were not confirmed on the current official pages.
reviews.evidenceText: Current LMUD pages document residential rebates for qualifying ENERGY STAR appliances, electric water heating, and air-source heat pumps; they do not clearly substantiate every technology mapped in the older opportunity record.

approvalRequirements: Be an eligible Massachusetts executive agency, state institution of higher education, or qualifying quasi-public state entity.
Propose restoration or replacement work on an eligible existing solar photovoltaic or decarbonized system within the current program scope.
Submit a complete Program Opportunity Notice response with the required site, technical, budget, schedule, and supporting documentation before work begins.
Receive Leading by Example and Department of Energy Resources award approval and execute the required grant documents.
Complete the approved work and satisfy invoicing, reporting, inspection, and closeout requirements.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: The current grant opportunity remains open through the published deadline, but applications require project-specific review and award approval and remain subject to available funding. Eligibility alone does not establish an entitlement.
reviews.evidenceText: The current Leading by Example restoration grant accepts eligible Massachusetts state-entity projects for existing solar and decarbonized systems through June 30, 2027, subject to application review and available funds.

approvalRequirements: Be an eligible Massachusetts executive agency, state institution of higher education, or qualifying quasi-public state entity.
Propose a project within the current solar-decarbonization grant scope, such as qualifying solar photovoltaic, storage, charging, or related enabling work.
Submit a complete rolling application with the required site, technical, budget, schedule, ownership, and supporting documentation before project commitment.
Receive Leading by Example and Department of Energy Resources award approval and execute the grant agreement.
Complete the approved project and satisfy invoicing, reporting, inspection, and closeout requirements.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: Applications are accepted and reviewed on a rolling basis, but awards depend on project-specific approval and the remaining allocation. A qualifying state project can compete for funding but is not guaranteed an award.
reviews.evidenceText: Massachusetts currently reviews eligible state-entity solar-decarbonization grant applications on a rolling basis through June 30, 2027, or until allocated funds are awarded.

approvalRequirements: Own an eligible privately held commercial, industrial, agricultural, multifamily, nonprofit, or other qualifying property in a participating Michigan jurisdiction.
Develop an eligible energy or water project supported by the required audit, energy model, savings analysis, and contractor scope.
Obtain private PACE lender underwriting and financing approval.
Secure written consent from each existing mortgage or lienholder when required.
Pass Lean & Green Michigan legal and program review, execute the Special Assessment Agreement, and obtain local-government approval and recording before closing.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: PACE eligibility does not guarantee financing. Closing depends on property and project economics, private-lender underwriting, lienholder consent, program compliance, executed legal documents, and local-government approval.
reviews.evidenceText: Lean & Green Michigan describes a privately financed commercial PACE process requiring an eligible property and project, technical analysis, lender approval, mortgage-holder consent, program review, a Special Assessment Agreement, and local approval.

approvalRequirements: Be an eligible applicant proposing new Level 2 charging at a qualifying Pennsylvania public, workplace, or multifamily location.
Meet the current equipment, plug, site, ownership, cost, and public-benefit requirements.
Apply and receive the Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Protection voucher before installing or committing the project.
Complete the approved installation within the voucher authorization period.
Submit the redemption package with invoices, payment evidence, equipment and site documentation, photographs, and any required verification.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: The current program operates as a rolling, first-come voucher rather than a scored competition. A qualifying project that secures a voucher before work and submits a complete redemption package is likely to receive the rebate while funding remains.
reviews.evidenceText: Pennsylvania currently offers rolling first-come Level 2 charging vouchers for eligible public, workplace, and multifamily projects, with installation and redemption documentation due within the approved voucher period.

approvalRequirements: Be an eligible Lewis County PUD commercial or industrial electric customer at the project site.
Contact PUD Energy Services and complete the required preproject review for the selected measure.
Complete an energy audit before weatherization work and obtain advance authorization for measures that require it.
Install equipment or building improvements that meet the current technical specifications and approved scope.
Submit final invoices, equipment and installation records, and savings information and pass any required inspection or verification.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: Lewis County PUD uses a defined utility project-review process rather than competitive ranking. A qualifying customer who completes required advance review, audit, installation, and closeout verification is likely to receive the incentive.
reviews.evidenceText: Current PUD materials require Energy Services coordination and an audit before commercial weatherization, and they provide project-specific incentives for qualifying commercial heat-pump and efficiency work.

approvalRequirements: Be an eligible Lewis County PUD residential electric customer at the installation address.
Select a current qualifying heat-pump, insulation, weatherization, or other listed residential measure.
Complete the required participation agreement or preproject authorization for the selected rebate pathway.
Complete an energy audit before weatherization work where required and install the measure to current specifications.
Submit invoices, model and installation records, and other requested documentation and pass any required verification or inspection.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: The PUD's residential rebates use published technical criteria and measure-specific forms. A qualifying installation that completes the required agreement, audit, and final documentation is likely to receive the incentive after verification.
reviews.evidenceText: Lewis County PUD currently requires an audit before residential weatherization and uses participation agreements, technical specifications, and installation documentation for residential heat-pump rebates.

approvalRequirements: Be an eligible Liberty Utilities Arkansas nonresidential electric customer for the project site.
Use a current prescriptive measure or develop a custom project that meets program technical and cost-effectiveness requirements.
Submit the applicable application, workbook, equipment specifications, costs, and savings documentation.
Obtain written preapproval before purchase or installation for custom projects and any other measure designated for advance review.
Complete the installation and submit final invoices, product records, and verification documents before incentive payment.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: The current program offers objective prescriptive incentives and a reviewed custom pathway. A qualifying prescriptive project, or a custom project that receives advance approval and passes final review, is likely to receive the incentive.
reviews.evidenceText: Liberty's current Arkansas commercial and industrial program provides prescriptive and custom incentives, requires preapproval for custom work, and requires application and completion documentation before payment.

approvalRequirements: Be an eligible Missouri Liberty natural-gas residential or qualifying small-firm customer on a covered rate.
Install a currently qualifying gas appliance, heating measure, thermostat, or approved home-performance improvement at the served property.
Provide a recent Liberty bill and use a separate current application for each rebate measure where required.
Submit paid invoices, model and efficiency information, contractor and installation records, and other requested documentation.
For the home-performance pathway, complete the required assessment and approved improvement process and allow verification before payment.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: Current Liberty Missouri materials provide objective gas-equipment and home-performance incentive pathways. A qualifying, documented measure is likely to be paid, but the current official sources do not support the older record's battery-storage mapping.
reviews.evidenceText: Liberty currently documents Missouri natural-gas equipment rebates and an assessed home-efficiency pathway for residential and qualifying small-firm customers; battery storage is not substantiated by the current program pages.

approvalRequirements: Be an eligible Liberty New Hampshire commercial electric customer in the applicable small- or large-business program track.
Submit the project application, proposed equipment, costs, technical information, and expected savings before installation.
Receive written preapproval and incentive reservation before purchasing or installing the project.
Satisfy any custom-project engineering and cost-effectiveness review.
Complete the authorized work and submit final invoices and completion documentation and pass any required inspection or verification.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: The current business programs state that preapproved incentives are reserved and use technical eligibility rather than competitive ranking. A qualifying project that follows the authorization and closeout process is likely to be paid while budget remains.
reviews.evidenceText: Liberty's current New Hampshire electric business programs require project submission and preapproval before installation, reserve approved incentive amounts, and require completion documentation and verification.

approvalRequirements: Be an eligible Liberty New Hampshire residential electric customer at the installation address.
Purchase and install a currently qualifying appliance, heating, cooling, water-heating, or other listed electric measure, or enroll an eligible home in the Home Energy Performance pathway.
For weatherization, complete the required program signup and in-home energy audit before the improvement scope is finalized.
Use required contractors and satisfy current equipment, installation, and efficiency specifications.
Submit the applicable application, invoices, model and installation records, and any required audit or verification documents while funds remain available.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: The current residential programs use objective measure specifications and a defined home-performance audit process. A qualifying customer who completes the applicable claim or approved weatherization pathway is likely to receive the incentive after review.
reviews.evidenceText: Liberty currently publishes New Hampshire residential electric rebates for qualifying equipment and a Home Energy Performance process that begins with signup and an in-home audit before weatherization incentives are determined.

approvalRequirements: Be an eligible Liberty New Hampshire commercial natural-gas customer for the project site.
Install a currently qualifying prescriptive gas measure or develop a custom project that satisfies technical and cost-effectiveness requirements.
Use a properly licensed contractor and comply with current equipment and installation specifications.
Complete any required prequalification, assessment, study, or advance project approval before commitment.
Submit the applicable post-installation application, paid invoices, equipment records, and verification documents while funds remain available.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: Liberty's current gas business offerings provide prescriptive rebates and reviewed custom or assessment pathways. A qualifying prescriptive installation or approved custom project is likely to receive the incentive after documentation review.
reviews.evidenceText: Current Liberty New Hampshire business gas materials cover qualifying heating, water-heating, controls, weatherization, and custom work, with prequalification for some pathways and post-installation forms for prescriptive rebates.

approvalRequirements: Be an eligible Liberty New Hampshire residential natural-gas customer at the installation address.
Install a currently qualifying furnace, boiler, water heater, thermostat, control, or other listed gas measure, or enroll an eligible home in the Home Energy Performance pathway.
Use a licensed contractor and satisfy the current equipment, efficiency, code, and installation requirements for equipment rebates.
For weatherization, complete program signup and the required in-home audit before the approved scope is established.
Submit the applicable application, invoices, model and installation records, and audit or verification documentation while funds remain available.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: The current gas residential programs use published equipment criteria and a defined home-performance audit pathway. A qualifying customer who submits complete documentation or completes the approved weatherization process is likely to receive the incentive.
reviews.evidenceText: Liberty currently offers New Hampshire residential gas equipment rebates and home-efficiency services, with licensed installation, claim documentation, signup, audit, and available-funding requirements depending on the measure.

approvalRequirements: Be a current or future Liberty Iowa customer on an eligible residential or small-commercial natural-gas rate.
Purchase and install a currently qualifying natural-gas appliance, heating system, or thermostat at an eligible property.
Use an appropriately qualified installer and comply with applicable codes and current product specifications.
Submit a separate current rebate form for each measure with a recent Liberty bill, paid invoice, model and efficiency information, and installation documentation.
Allow Liberty to review or inspect the installation before payment while rebate funding remains available.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: The current Iowa rebate uses objective customer, rate, equipment, and documentation criteria. A qualifying installation with complete paperwork is likely to be paid after routine review, subject to the available program budget.
reviews.evidenceText: Liberty currently offers Iowa high-efficiency natural-gas equipment rebates to eligible residential and small-commercial rate classes and requires separate forms, a recent bill, complete purchase and installation records, and code-compliant work.

approvalRequirements: No new application can currently be approved because the Texas Commission on Environmental Quality marks the Light-Duty Motor Vehicle Purchase or Lease Incentive Program as closed.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: TCEQ currently lists the program as closed, so a new applicant has no active award pathway unless a future funding round opens. The program concerns eligible light-duty vehicle purchases, leases, or conversion systems and does not support the mapped stationary fuel-cell retrofit.
reviews.evidenceText: TCEQ currently identifies the light-duty vehicle incentive as closed. Its eligible activity is alternative-fuel vehicle acquisition or conversion rather than a stationary fuel-cell energy system.
